Audi's Next RS6 Spied in Sedan Flavor Lapping the Nurburgring Nordschleife
12 photos
Photo: Baldauf
Audi's 2028 model year RS 6 is right around the corner. Spied at the Nordschleife in four-door guise, the V8-powered thriller is wearing production-intent bodywork under a great deal of camouflage wrap. Curiously, the camo fails to hide the underlying blue paintwork. Its front and rear fenders, along with the bumpers, have grown more aggressive from the six-cylinder S6.
The widebody aesthetic with look-at-me intakes up front is complemented by a redesigned bumper out back, which incorporates two exhaust outlets with an oval design. Previously rumored to feature a reworked 2.9-liter V6 from the RS 4/RS 5, which Audi might have tested at some point, the RS 6 is actually packing the 4.0-liter V8 we all know and love. That's not all, though.
On the right-side rear quarter panel, we can see the fuel filler door. Opposite, the German automaker integrated the charging port on the driver-side rear quarter panel. That port is connected to a high-voltage battery, though exact details remain unknown. Because it's related to the RS 5 under the skin, prospective customers may be presented with 25.9 kWh gross at the very least.
Audi claims just around 22 kilowatt-hours net, with the battery located under the trunk floor. Its charging system supports up to 11 kilowatts on AC, and curiously enough, DC fast charging is not supported. Regarding electric motor integration, Audi took inspiration from BMW's M5 sedan and wagon.
More specifically, the RS 5 uses a hybridized ZF eight-speed automatic. The P2 layout should carry over to the RS 6, with P2 meaning electric motor housed between the transmission and engine, inside the bell housing. A separating clutch disconnects the internal combustion engine so the vehicle can be driven on pure electric power without any kind of engine drag.
Photo: Baldauf These latest spy photos of the 2028 model year RS 6 also reveal that Audi has decided on a four-door body rather than five doors for the RS 5 sedan. Indeed, the RS 5 is a liftback by default. It's been 16 years since the C6-generation RS 6 sedan left us, with remaining stock lasting until 2011.
With the C9 generation, Audi will restore the choice between sedan and longroof. Definitely benchmarked against the BMW M5 Sedan and Touring, the RS 6 is certain to exceed 700 horsepower and 700 pound-feet (950 Newton-meters) at full throttle, even with Euro 7 regs knocking at the door.
The RS 6 should also borrow quattro with Dynamic Torque Control from the RS 5, specifically an all-wheel-drive system with an electromechanical torque-vectoring rear differential. Instead of hydraulic clutches, a water-cooled electric actuator that runs at 400 volts does the heavy lifting.
Because it operates independently of the engine, said permanent-magnet actuator can shift a lot of torque to the outside rear wheel to help the car turn sharper. Wider than the S6, the RS 6 retains the full-width LED taillight setup of lesser A6 family members.
The standard light bar features choreographed unlocking and locking animations, while the available OLED lights double as an external display. All segments automatically illuminate at full brightness when another vehicle approaches within two meters of a stationary A6 optioned with these lights.
Visually distinct from the poor-selling RS e-tron GT and the S6 e-tron , the RS 6 will reach US dealers in both sedan and Avant body styles. Confirmation came from none other than Audi of America product chief Filip Brabec, who cited strong demand for the outgoing RS 6 Avant as the reason for the automaker's decision to continue selling the wagon stateside.
